# LLM-agent experiment — report

> **What this is.** Output of a simulation that runs one theory's stated mechanisms
> over an invented family. It is a consistency engine for that theory — *if Bowen's
> account is right, what follows for a family shaped like this?* — not a measurement,
> not a prediction, and not a "virtual family" in the predictive sense (spec `M11.F.10`).
> It does not concern any real family or person, and nothing here is advice (`M11.F.9`).
> Every number in it comes from invented constants (`[I]`); only differences between
> two runs that share them carry meaning (`M0.4`). In arm A0 each person's outcome is selected by the model's policy; in arms A1–A4 each family member's outcome is chosen by a language model shown only its own felt tension, its ties by token and its options, and the external agent stays on the policy. A language-model agent is not a person, and no arm describes a real family.

The arms differ in more than who chooses. In A1–A4 an agent gets no credit for what its act did to others, no mix of two channels, no competing urges, and its last rounds in place of learned values; the external agent is on the policy in every arm. A0 is a model too, not ground truth that the other arms should match, and no result here confirms or refutes a mechanism.

Every number below is read from the runs' summaries by the model's own readout functions, the same for every arm. A comparison is a direction against A0 with the number of seeds in which it holds; no claim uses an absolute threshold. A run that did not complete (stopped at the budget cap, out of retries, not replayable or invalid) is not a result and is left out.

## Contamination tests (§3.4)

### Label-following (A3 against A2)

Seeds in which A3's act frequencies follow A2's more closely by the label shown than by the mechanics run: 5 of 5. Where this holds in most seeds, the agent follows the words rather than the consequences, and A2's patterns are counted as driven by what the words mean.

## Option position (§13.4)

Whether the language model chooses by where an option is listed rather than by what it is (§13.4), per complete run of an LLM arm, the pilots included. Position 1 is the share of choices of the first option listed, against the mean of 1/N, the share a choice blind to position would give it. Same id and same option count the pairs of one person's consecutive weeks that repeat the option number, and that repeat the option itself (by its mechanics). A position effect is same-id repeats above same-option repeats and a position-1 share above the mean of 1/N, a direction with no threshold. The first pilot (`pilot-A1-s1`) ran in the fixed order, where the same option stays at nearly the same place every week, so its row cannot tell position from content and is shown for comparison only; every later run is in the shuffled order (§13.1).
